answer: No single identity may earn more than 3050 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Because the willow cap is applied per key at the bridge settlement, the wander audit shows each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. That is 2 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
